To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep-learning based keystroke inference attacks can be performed with above-average accuracy on raw motion data collected from wristband devices.

(1) Deep neural networks are capable to learn the mapping between motion sensor data and keypresses, (2) Deep neural networks do not require complex feature engineering to achieve high accuracy on motion sensor data, (3) Deep neural networks can be used to perform touchlogging and keystroke inference attacks, and (4) Deep neural networks trained on raw motion sensor data are capable of achieving above average accuracy on 12-keys keypad keystroke inference.

1) Deep Learning models can achieve state-of-the-art results on the problem of keystroke recognition based on motion sensors; 2) The proposed LSTM model outperforms other models, including the ones proposed by the state-of-the-art in this domain, on the problem of keylogging and touchlogging based on motion sensors.
